chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:

There is many a man being gradually brought towards punishment by good treatment with him; many a man who remains in deceit because his evils are covered; and many a man who is in illusion because of good talk about him, while there is no greater ordeal by Allāh, the Glorified, than the giving of time.

key_terms.الْإِمْلَاءِ: Giving time or breathing space (to the sinner)
key_terms.مَفْتُونٍ: One who is enchanted or deluded
key_terms.مُسْتَدْرَجٍ: One who is gradually led on or insidiously drawn towards punishment

ai.seo_question: What is meant by 'al-imla' (giving time) as a divine trial in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) elucidates the concept of *al-imla'* (divine breathing space), where God grants sinners prolonged indulgence in worldly comforts as a subtle trial rather than immediate retribution. This period of 'gradual leading to ruin' serves to deepen their arrogance and ensure that when punishment finally arrives, it is comprehensive and inescapable. This concept is central to Shia exegesis of divine justice, illustrating how mercy can sometimes mask a severe test of endurance.

en.sayed-ali-raza: 260. Amīr al-mu’minīn, peace be upon him, said:

There is many a man being gradually brought towards punishment by good treatment with him; many a man who remains in deceit because his evils are covered; and many a man who is in illusion because of good talk about him, while there is no greater ordeal by Allāh, the Glorified, than the giving of time.
